matches.label: Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood
matches.note: Noah and his people before the flood: Gen records no word from Noah, only obedience (wayyaʿaś nōaḥ kᵉkōl ʾăšer-ṣiwwāhû YHWH); Q adds a long debate, innī lakum nadhīrun mubīnun an lā taʿbudū illā llāha, with the chiefs' replies (mā narāka illā basharan mithlanā) and their mockery while he builds (sakhirū minhu).

passages.text: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ נֹ֑חַ כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֥ה אֹת֛וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים כֵּ֥ן עָשָֽׂה
וַיַּ֖עַשׂ נֹ֑חַ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֖הוּ יְהוָֽה
وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنِّى لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ
أَن لَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ

فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرًا مِّثْلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِىَ ٱلرَّأْىِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِن فَضْلٍۭ بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كَٰذِبِينَ

matches.label: Why God destroyed a generation or a people
matches.note: Why they drown: Gen, the earth full of violence (kî-mālᵉʾāh hāʾāreṣ ḥāmās mippᵉnêhem); Q, rejecting the messenger and doing wrong (lladhīna ẓalamū innahum mughraqūn), after Noah's preaching. In Gen all flesh perishes (qēṣ kol-bāśār); in Q 'Noah's people'.

passages.text: וַתִּשָּׁחֵ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ לִפְנֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַתִּמָּלֵ֥א הָאָ֖רֶץ חָמָֽס
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְנֹ֗חַ קֵ֤ץ כָּל בָּשָׂר֙ בָּ֣א לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ חָמָ֖ס מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהִנְנִ֥י מַשְׁחִיתָ֖ם אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ

فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرًا مِّثْلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِىَ ٱلرَّأْىِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِن فَضْلٍۭ بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كَٰذِبِينَ
وَٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

matches.label: When and from where the flood waters come
matches.note: The sign that the flood begins: ḥattā idhā jāʾa amrunā wa-fāra t-tannūru (the oven boiled over) vs bayyôm hazzeh nibqᵉʿû kol-maʿyᵉnōt tᵉhôm rabbāh waʾărubbōt haššāmayim niptāḥû, dated to the 17th of the second month of Noah's 600th year. Q has a domestic oven instead of the cosmic deep and the windows of heaven, and no date. cf. b. Sanhedrin 108b (boiling flood waters), outside the canon.

passages.text: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שֵׁשׁ מֵא֤וֹת שָׁנָה֙ לְחַיֵּי נֹ֔חַ בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָֽה עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה נִבְקְעוּ֙ כָּֽל מַעְיְנֹת֙ תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֔ה וַאֲרֻבֹּ֥ת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם נִפְתָּֽחוּ

حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ قُلْنَا ٱحْمِلْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ وَمَنْ ءَامَنَ وَمَآ ءَامَنَ مَعَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ

matches.label: Which of Noah's household enter the ark and survive
matches.note: The household on board: Gen has all of Noah's family, by name, eight persons (bāʾ nōaḥ wᵉšēm wᵉḥām wāyepet bᵉnê-nōaḥ wᵉʾēšet nōaḥ ûšᵉlōšet nᵉšê-bānāyw); Q has his family 'except the one against whom the word went before' plus the few believers (wa-ahlaka illā man sabaqa ʿalayhi l-qawlu wa-man āmana wa-mā āmana maʿahu illā qalīl). One son refuses, is called in vain (yā bunayya rkab maʿanā) and drowns (fa-kāna mina l-mughraqīn).

passages.text: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֥י אֶת בְּרִיתִ֖י אִתָּ֑ךְ וּבָאתָ֙ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֔ה אַתָּ֕ה וּבָנֶ֛יךָ וְאִשְׁתְּךָ֥ וּנְשֵֽׁי בָנֶ֖יךָ אִתָּֽךְ
בְּעֶ֨צֶם הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ בָּ֣א נֹ֔חַ וְשֵׁם וְחָ֥ם וָיֶ֖פֶת בְּנֵי נֹ֑חַ וְאֵ֣שֶׁת נֹ֗חַ וּשְׁלֹ֧שֶׁת נְשֵֽׁי בָנָ֛יו אִתָּ֖ם אֶל הַתֵּבָֽה

حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ قُلْنَا ٱحْمِلْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ وَمَنْ ءَامَنَ وَمَآ ءَامَنَ مَعَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ
وَهِىَ تَجْرِى بِهِمْ فِى مَوْجٍ كَٱلْجِبَالِ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبْنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِى مَعْزِلٍ يَٰبُنَىَّ ٱرْكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
قَالَ سَـَٔاوِىٓ إِلَىٰ جَبَلٍ يَعْصِمُنِى مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ قَالَ لَا عَاصِمَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مِنْ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَ وَحَالَ بَيْنَهُمَا ٱلْمَوْجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُغْرَقِينَ

matches.label: How the flood waters are stopped and subside
matches.note: Earth and sky are both stopped: yā arḍu blaʿī māʾaki wa-yā samāʾu aqliʿī wa-ghīḍa l-māʾu vs wayyissākᵉrû maʿyᵉnōt tᵉhôm waʾărubbōt haššāmayim wayyikkālēʾ haggešem ... wayyaʿăbēr ʾĕlōhîm rûaḥ ... wayyāšōkkû hammāyim. Changed: God commands the earth and the sky directly by word in Q; in Gen he sends a wind and the waters recede slowly over 150 days.

passages.text: וַיִּזְכֹּ֤ר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת נֹ֔חַ וְאֵ֤ת כָּל הַֽחַיָּה֙ וְאֶת כָּל הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּתֵּבָ֑ה וַיַּעֲבֵ֨ר אֱלֹהִ֥ים ר֨וּחַ֙ עַל הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיָּשֹׁ֖כּוּ הַמָּֽיִם
וַיִּסָּֽכְרוּ֙ מַעְיְנֹ֣ת תְּה֔וֹם וַֽאֲרֻבֹּ֖ת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַיִּכָּלֵ֥א הַגֶּ֖שֶׁם מִן הַשָּׁמָֽיִם
וַיָּשֻׁ֧בוּ הַמַּ֛יִם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָ֖רֶץ הָל֣וֹךְ וָשׁ֑וֹב וַיַּחְסְר֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם מִקְצֵ֕ה חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת יֽוֹם
وَقِيلَ يَٰٓأَرْضُ ٱبْلَعِى مَآءَكِ وَيَٰسَمَآءُ أَقْلِعِى وَغِيضَ ٱلْمَآءُ وَقُضِىَ ٱلْأَمْرُ وَٱسْتَوَتْ عَلَى ٱلْجُودِىِّ وَقِيلَ بُعْدًا لِّلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

matches.label: Vessel comes to rest on a named mountain
matches.note: The landing place: wa-stawat ʿalā l-jūdiyyi vs wattānaḥ hattēbāh ... ʿal hārê ʾărārāṭ. A different mountain; cf. Targum Onqelos and the Peshitta on Gen 8:4 (Qardu), outside the Hebrew text.

passages.text: וַתָּ֤נַח הַתֵּבָה֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ עַ֖ל הָרֵ֥י אֲרָרָֽט
وَقِيلَ يَٰٓأَرْضُ ٱبْلَعِى مَآءَكِ وَيَٰسَمَآءُ أَقْلِعِى وَغِيضَ ٱلْمَآءُ وَقُضِىَ ٱلْأَمْرُ وَٱسْتَوَتْ عَلَى ٱلْجُودِىِّ وَقِيلَ بُعْدًا لِّلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

matches.label: Whether and how Noah speaks to God
matches.note: Noah never speaks to God in Gen; he obeys and offers sacrifice (wayyiben nōaḥ mizbēaḥ laYHWH). In Q he calls to God for his drowned son (rabbi inna bnī min ahlī wa-inna waʿdaka l-ḥaqq), is rebuked, and asks for refuge and forgiveness.

passages.text: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ נֹ֑חַ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֖הוּ יְהוָֽה
וַיִּ֥בֶן נֹ֛חַ מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֞ח מִכֹּ֣ל הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה הַטְּהוֹרָ֗ה וּמִכֹּל֙ הָע֣וֹף הַטָּהֹ֔ר וַיַּ֥עַל עֹלֹ֖ת בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ
وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ رَّبَّهُۥ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ ٱبْنِى مِنْ أَهْلِى وَإِنَّ وَعْدَكَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَأَنتَ أَحْكَمُ ٱلْحَٰكِمِينَ
قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّىٓ أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ أَسْـَٔلَكَ مَا لَيْسَ لِى بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ وَإِلَّا تَغْفِرْ لِى وَتَرْحَمْنِىٓ أَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ

matches.label: Noah's standing before God: blameless, or in need of forgiveness
matches.note: Noah's standing: Gen calls him nōaḥ ʾîš ṣaddîq tāmîm ... ʾet-hāʾĕlōhîm hithallek-nōaḥ; in Q he is warned not to be among the ignorant (innī aʿiẓuka an takūna mina l-jāhilīn) and pleads wa-illā taghfir lī wa-tarḥamnī akun mina l-khāsirīn.

passages.text: אֵ֚לֶּה תּוֹלְדֹ֣ת נֹ֔חַ נֹ֗חַ אִ֥ישׁ צַדִּ֛יק תָּמִ֥ים הָיָ֖ה בְּדֹֽרֹתָ֑יו אֶת הָֽאֱלֹהִ֖ים הִֽתְהַלֶּךְ נֹֽחַ
قَالَ يَٰنُوحُ إِنَّهُۥ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ إِنَّهُۥ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صَٰلِحٍ فَلَا تَسْـَٔلْنِ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ إِنِّىٓ أَعِظُكَ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ
قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّىٓ أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ أَسْـَٔلَكَ مَا لَيْسَ لِى بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ وَإِلَّا تَغْفِرْ لِى وَتَرْحَمْنِىٓ أَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ

matches.label: What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest
matches.note: After the landing: Gen, Noah builds an altar and offers burnt offerings whose scent God smells (wayyāraḥ YHWH ʾet-rêaḥ hannîḥōaḥ); Q has no sacrifice, only a divine command and blessing: yā nūḥu hbiṭ bi-salāmin minnā wa-barakātin ʿalayka wa-ʿalā umamin mimman maʿak.

passages.text: וַיִּ֥בֶן נֹ֛חַ מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֞ח מִכֹּ֣ל הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה הַטְּהוֹרָ֗ה וּמִכֹּל֙ הָע֣וֹף הַטָּהֹ֔ר וַיַּ֥עַל עֹלֹ֖ת בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ

וַיָּ֣רַח יְהוָה֮ אֶת רֵ֣יחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל לִבּ֗וֹ לֹֽא אֹ֠סִף לְקַלֵּ֨ל ע֤וֹד אֶת הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּעֲב֣וּר הָֽאָדָ֔ם כִּ֠י יֵ֣צֶר לֵ֧ב הָאָדָ֛ם רַ֖ע מִנְּעֻרָ֑יו וְלֹֽא אֹסִ֥ף ע֛וֹד לְהַכּ֥וֹת אֶת כָּל חַ֖י כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִֽׂיתִי
قِيلَ يَٰنُوحُ ٱهْبِطْ بِسَلَٰمٍ مِّنَّا وَبَرَكَٰتٍ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ أُمَمٍ مِّمَّن مَّعَكَ وَأُمَمٌ سَنُمَتِّعُهُمْ ثُمَّ يَمَسُّهُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ

matches.label: What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come
matches.note: God's word about later generations is opposite: Gen promises no repeat (lōʾ-ʾōsip ʿôd lᵉhakkôt ʾet-kol-ḥay kaʾăšer ʿāśîtî), because the human heart is evil from youth; Q announces that some later nations will enjoy life and then be punished again (wa-umamun sa-numattiʿuhum thumma yamassuhum minnā ʿadhābun alīm).

passages.text: וַיָּ֣רַח יְהוָה֮ אֶת רֵ֣יחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל לִבּ֗וֹ לֹֽא אֹ֠סִף לְקַלֵּ֨ל ע֤וֹד אֶת הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּעֲב֣וּר הָֽאָדָ֔ם כִּ֠י יֵ֣צֶר לֵ֧ב הָאָדָ֛ם רַ֖ע מִנְּעֻרָ֑יו וְלֹֽא אֹסִ֥ף ע֛וֹד לְהַכּ֥וֹת אֶת כָּל חַ֖י כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִֽׂיתִי
قِيلَ يَٰنُوحُ ٱهْبِطْ بِسَلَٰمٍ مِّنَّا وَبَرَكَٰتٍ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ أُمَمٍ مِّمَّن مَّعَكَ وَأُمَمٌ سَنُمَتِّعُهُمْ ثُمَّ يَمَسُّهُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ

matches.label: Hero privately warned of the coming flood by a deity
matches.note: God tells Noah privately that the others will be destroyed by water: wa-ūḥiya ilā nūḥin annahu lan yuʾmina min qawmika illā man qad āmana ... innahum mughraqūn vs qēṣ kol-bāśār bāʾ lᵉpānay ... hinnî mēbîʾ ʾet-hammabbûl mayim.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְנֹ֗חַ קֵ֤ץ כָּל בָּשָׂר֙ בָּ֣א לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ חָמָ֖ס מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהִנְנִ֥י מַשְׁחִיתָ֖ם אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ
וַאֲנִ֗י הִנְנִי֩ מֵבִ֨יא אֶת הַמַּבּ֥וּל מַ֨יִם֙ עַל הָאָ֔רֶץ לְשַׁחֵ֣ת כָּל בָּשָׂ֗ר אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ֙ ר֣וּחַ חַיִּ֔ים מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר בָּאָ֖רֶץ יִגְוָֽע
وَأُوحِىَ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ أَنَّهُۥ لَن يُؤْمِنَ مِن قَوْمِكَ إِلَّا مَن قَدْ ءَامَنَ فَلَا تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَفْعَلُونَ
وَٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

matches.label: Hero builds a vessel on divine instruction
matches.note: wa-ṣnaʿi l-fulka bi-aʿyuninā wa-waḥyinā vs ʿăśēh lᵉkā tēbat ʿăṣê-gōper. Gen gives the material, measurements and pitch (6:14-16); Q only 'under our eyes and our inspiration'.

passages.text: עֲשֵׂ֤ה לְךָ֙ תֵּבַ֣ת עֲצֵי גֹ֔פֶר קִנִּ֖ים תַּֽעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֶת הַתֵּבָ֑ה וְכָֽפַרְתָּ֥ אֹתָ֛הּ מִבַּ֥יִת וּמִח֖וּץ בַּכֹּֽפֶר
وَٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ
وَيَصْنَعُ ٱلْفُلْكَ وَكُلَّمَا مَرَّ عَلَيْهِ مَلَأٌ مِّن قَوْمِهِۦ سَخِرُوا۟ مِنْهُ قَالَ إِن تَسْخَرُوا۟ مِنَّا فَإِنَّا نَسْخَرُ مِنكُمْ كَمَا تَسْخَرُونَ

matches.label: Animals taken aboard in pairs
matches.note: min kullin zawjayni thnayni vs šᵉnayim mikkōl ... zākār ûnᵉqēbāh. Q lacks Gen's second rule of seven pairs of clean animals (šibʿāh šibʿāh, Gen 7:2).

passages.text: וּמִכָּל הָ֠חַי מִֽכָּל בָּשָׂ֞ר שְׁנַ֧יִם מִכֹּ֛ל תָּבִ֥יא אֶל הַתֵּבָ֖ה לְהַחֲיֹ֣ת אִתָּ֑ךְ זָכָ֥ר וּנְקֵבָ֖ה יִֽהְיֽוּ
מִכֹּ֣ל הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה הַטְּהוֹרָ֗ה תִּֽקַּח לְךָ֛ שִׁבְעָ֥ה שִׁבְעָ֖ה אִ֣ישׁ וְאִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וּמִן הַבְּהֵמָ֡ה אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹ֣א טְהֹרָ֥ה הִ֛וא שְׁנַ֖יִם אִ֥ישׁ וְאִשְׁתּֽוֹ

حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ قُلْنَا ٱحْمِلْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ وَمَنْ ءَامَنَ وَمَآ ءَامَنَ مَعَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ

matches.label: Waters rise above the highest mountains (fifteen cubits)
matches.note: No mountain gives refuge from the flood: saʾāwī ilā jabalin yaʿṣimunī mina l-māʾi qāla lā ʿāṣima l-yawma min amri llāh; fī mawjin ka-l-jibāl vs wayᵉkussû kol-hehārîm haggᵉbōhîm ... ḥămēš ʿeśrēh ʾammāh milmaʿlāh.

passages.text: וְהַמַּ֗יִם גָּֽבְר֛וּ מְאֹ֥ד מְאֹ֖ד עַל הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיְכֻסּ֗וּ כָּל הֶֽהָרִים֙ הַגְּבֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר תַּ֖חַת כָּל הַשָּׁמָֽיִם
חֲמֵ֨שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה אַמָּה֙ מִלְמַ֔עְלָה גָּבְר֖וּ הַמָּ֑יִם וַיְכֻסּ֖וּ הֶהָרִֽים
وَهِىَ تَجْرِى بِهِمْ فِى مَوْجٍ كَٱلْجِبَالِ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبْنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِى مَعْزِلٍ يَٰبُنَىَّ ٱرْكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
قَالَ سَـَٔاوِىٓ إِلَىٰ جَبَلٍ يَعْصِمُنِى مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ قَالَ لَا عَاصِمَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مِنْ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَ وَحَالَ بَيْنَهُمَا ٱلْمَوْجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُغْرَقِينَ

Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi

matches.label: A son of Noah is found unworthy, and what follows
matches.note: One of Noah's sons is rejected: in Gen, Ham, after the flood, sees his father's nakedness and his son Canaan is cursed (ʾārûr kᵉnāʿan ʿebed ʿăbādîm yihyeh lᵉʾeḥāyw); in Q an unnamed son refuses the ark, drowns before the end of the flood, and God declares him 'not of your family, a deed not righteous' (innahu laysa min ahlika innahu ʿamalun ghayru ṣāliḥ). leads.title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ The Book made firm, the Throne on the water, the challenge of ten surahs
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 same element, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God lays the beams of his upper chambers on the (heavenly) waters and waters the mountains from them (weight 7.7); All creatures look to God to give their food in due season; he opens his hand and they are satisfied (weight 6.8). Pair score 14.6.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; God looks at the earth and it trembles, touches the mountains and they smoke; and 39 more.

Only in The Book made firm, the Throne on the water, the challenge of ten surahs: Every creature on earth has its provision from God, who knows its resting place and depository; Before creation God's throne was upon the water; On judgment day witnesses (al-ashhad) testify against those who lied about God; Those who want only this life are paid in full here and have nothing in the hereafter but fire; God created heaven and earth to test which of you is best in deeds; Deniers demand that a treasure be sent down to the prophet or an angel come with him; A divine wind or spirit hovers or moves over the primeval waters; YHWH sat enthroned over the flood (mabbul); YHWH sits as king forever; God sets each creature in its place, supplies its sustenance and knows (reckons) its term or abode; Man calls on God lying, sitting or standing in distress, then passes on as if he had never prayed once relieved; Moses writes the Torah and gives it to the Levitical priests and elders; What is over the waters before or at creation: God's spirit, his throne or his voice [divergence between the texts]; and 11 more.

leads.title: Psalm 11 - in YHWH I take refuge ↔ Lot, his guests, his daughters and the stones of sijjil
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities (weight 5.9). Pair score 5.9.

Only in Psalm 11 - in YHWH I take refuge: The righteous is told to flee like a bird to the mountain; If the foundations (shatot) are destroyed, what can the righteous do?; God's throne is in heaven; his eyes behold and his eyelids test humankind; The upright shall behold God's face; The wicked bend the bow and fit the arrow to shoot the upright in darkness; Angels drag the sinner into the midst of hellfire and pour boiling water (hamim) over his head; The 'frequented House' (al-bayt al-ma'mur), understood as a heavenly sanctuary above the Ka'ba visited by angels; God rains coals, fire, sulfur and scorching wind on the wicked as the portion of their cup; Superscription 'for the leader/choirmaster' (lamenatseah).

Only in Lot, his guests, his daughters and the stones of sijjil: The angels tell Lot the destruction is appointed for the morning: 'is not the morning near?'; Lot wishes he had strength or a strong support to take refuge in; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; A dwelling or town is overturned so that its top and bottom are exchanged; Only Lot's household is brought out of the doomed city; What Lot says to the townsmen; How Lot receives the heavenly guests [divergence between the texts]; A protected person is forbidden to look out or turn round, and one does [divergence between the texts]; The deity rains stones from heaven on those he destroys: what kind of stones [divergence between the texts]; When Lot leaves the city and when the destruction falls [divergence between the texts]; Lot's townspeople turn on him; What falls from heaven on Sodom; and 11 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Perform prayer at the two ends of the day and in the near hours of the night (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Psalm 55, wings of a dove and the treacherous friend: Men of blood and deceit will not live out half their days; Cast your burden on YHWH and he will sustain you; Wish for wings like a dove to fly away and rest in the wilderness; Wish that the enemies go down alive into Sheol; Guard the prayers and the middle prayer (al-salat al-wusta); A man whose speech pleases, who calls God to witness, but goes forth to destroy tillage and offspring; Speaker betrayed not by an enemy but by an intimate companion with whom he shared counsel in God's house; God confuses human language; Enemy's words are smoother than butter or oil but are drawn swords; The wicked are brought down to the pit (be'er shahat / bor), the underworld; Prayer at evening, morning and noon (three fixed times a day); Glorify God in the evening, morning, afternoon and noon (set times of praise or prayer); and 1 more.

Only in Stand firm; prayer times; good deeds remove bad: Only a few in past generations forbade corruption, and they were saved; The stories of the messengers are told to make the prophet's heart firm; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; Humankind was originally one community, then they differed; Hero challenges God: shall the judge of all the earth not do justice? [response between the texts]; When a land is destroyed only the righteous few are rescued, by their own righteousness; Whether the god destroys a city whose people do right [divergence between the texts]; Good deeds remove evil deeds; Hero bargains with God to spare a city for the sake of a few righteous (50 down to 10); Prophet tells deniers 'Wait, I too am waiting'.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Why God destroyed a generation or a people (weight 7.3); Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood (weight 6.8); Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood (weight 6.2); Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger (weight 5.9); The Prophet asks no wage for the message (weight 5.7); Hero's family saved with him (weight 5.4). passages.text: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ خَلَٰٓئِفَ وَأَغْرَقْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ

sides.note: Why the generation drowns: in Q because they rejected the messenger (wa-aghraqnā lladhīna kadhdhabū bi-āyātinā); in Gen because the earth was full of violence and corruption (wattimmālēʾ hāʾāreṣ ḥāmās ... kî-hišḥît kol-bāśār ʾet-darkô). Moral corruption becomes rejection of a prophet.

passages.text: فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرًا مِّثْلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِىَ ٱلرَّأْىِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِن فَضْلٍۭ بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كَٰذِبِينَ
وَٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

sides.note: Why they drown: Gen, the earth full of violence (kî-mālᵉʾāh hāʾāreṣ ḥāmās mippᵉnêhem); Q, rejecting the messenger and doing wrong (lladhīna ẓalamū innahum mughraqūn), after Noah's preaching. In Gen all flesh perishes (qēṣ kol-bāśār); in Q 'Noah's people'.

فَإِن تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَمَا سَأَلْتُكُم مِّنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ

sides.note: Noah before the flood: in Gen he says nothing to anyone and simply obeys (wayyaʿaś nōaḥ kᵉkōl ʾăšer ṣiwwāh ʾōtô ʾĕlōhîm kēn ʿāśāh); in Q he preaches and challenges his people: yā qawmi in kāna kabura ʿalaykum maqāmī wa-tadhkīrī bi-āyāti llāhi ... fa-ajmiʿū amrakum wa-shurakāʾakum. passages.text: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنِّى لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ

فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرًا مِّثْلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِىَ ٱلرَّأْىِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِن فَضْلٍۭ بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كَٰذِبِينَ

sides.note: Noah and his people before the flood: Gen records no word from Noah, only obedience (wayyaʿaś nōaḥ kᵉkōl ʾăšer-ṣiwwāhû YHWH); Q adds a long debate, innī lakum nadhīrun mubīnun an lā taʿbudū illā llāha, with the chiefs' replies (mā narāka illā basharan mithlanā) and their mockery while he builds (sakhirū minhu).

فَقَرَّبَهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ

sides.note: a fattened calf ('ijl samin)

matches.label: A guest refuses to sit on the chair offered, to touch the table or to put his lip to the cup

passages.text: وَلَقَدْ جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَآ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ بِٱلْبُشْرَىٰ قَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًا قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ فَمَا لَبِثَ أَن جَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ حَنِيذٍ
فَلَمَّا رَءَآ أَيْدِيَهُمْ لَا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهِ نَكِرَهُمْ وَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّآ أُرْسِلْنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِ لُوطٍ

sides.note: The guest does not sit, does not go to the table, does not put his lip to the cup (§3:15-20); Abraham's guests' hands do not reach the calf (lā taṣilu ilayhi), and he mistrusts them.

passages.text: فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِۦ فَجَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ
فَقَرَّبَهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ

sides.note: The host's question to the guest who will not eat: 'why do you not eat ... why do you not drink, my lord?' against fa-qarrabahu ilayhim qāla a-lā taʾkulūn. Who the refusing guest is, is broken in the Hittite. 51:24-27 is not in the list of candidates: I add it here.

passages.text: فَلَمَّا رَءَآ أَيْدِيَهُمْ لَا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهِ نَكِرَهُمْ وَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّآ أُرْسِلْنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِ لُوطٍ

sides.note: contrast Gen 18:8 where they eat

passages.text: إِذْ دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًا قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونَ
فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِۦ فَجَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ
فَقَرَّبَهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ

sides.note: A chair is set for the Sun god and he does not sit (UL ešat), a table is laid and he does not come near (UL šalikta), a cup is given and he does not put his lip to it; the storm god asks whether the chamberlain, table servant or cupbearer was at fault 'so that you did not eat (UL ezatta)?'. 51:26-28: Abraham brings a fat calf, sets it near them, 'will you not eat? (a-lā taʾkulūn)', and fears them. Both guests then state their errand: the Sun god the monster in the sea, the envoys a son and a doomed people (51:28-32).

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The old wife overhears the promise of a son at the tent door and laughs (weight 7.3); A tender calf is slaughtered and served to divine guests (weight 7.3); A guest refuses to sit on the chair offered, to touch the table or to put his lip to the cup (weight 7.3); Abraham's angelic guests do not stretch their hands to the food, and he is afraid (weight 7.3); Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them (weight 5.8). Pair score 35.2.

Only in Abraham's guests, the roasted calf and the laughing wife: Abraham is forbearing, sighing (awwah) and penitent; The annunciation names Isaac 'and after Isaac, Jacob'; Promised son born to aged parents at the appointed time; Whether the divine guest eats the meal prepared by the host [divergence between the texts]; Doubt voiced at the promise of a son in old age; Who is afraid during the visit of the heavenly guests, and why [divergence between the texts]; How Abraham learns of Sodom's fate, and his response; Who Abraham's visitors are; A host sets meat before an arriving messenger, who does not take the meal, and fear follows [divergence between the texts]; How God answers Abraham's plea for the people of Sodom [divergence between the texts]; An intercessor pleads with the divine to spare a city whose destruction is decreed; the decree is not turned back [divergence between the texts]; When and why Sarah laughs, and how it is answered; and 9 more.

Only in Abraham's honored guests, the barren old wife striking her face, the stones of clay for Lot's people; Pharaoh, 'Ad, Thamud and Noah: On 'Ad God sent the barren wind (al-rih al-'aqim), which left everything like rotten bones; Abraham brings a fattened calf but the guests do not eat, and he becomes afraid of them; The honored guests enter saying 'Peace' and Abraham replies 'Peace, strangers (qawm munkarun)'; The guests announce to Abraham a knowing (or wise) son ('alim); Thamud were told 'Enjoy yourselves for a while', defied the command and were seized by the thunderbolt while they looked on; Abraham's wife comes forward crying out, strikes her face and says 'A barren old woman!'; Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; The answer given to the old woman's doubt [divergence between the texts]; Supernatural envoys who come to seize or destroy do not eat the food offered them [divergence between the texts]; Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them [divergence between the texts]; The host, seeing the divine visitor, has his household prepare an animal from the herd (lamb, calf) for the guest; How Abraham learns of Sodom's fate, and his response [divergence between the texts]; and 20 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Stones of baked clay (sijjil), in layers, each marked by the Lord, rain on the town (weight 7.3); Not looking back when leaving behind the doomed place or the banished evil [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); Lot's wife is among those who stay behind and perish (weight 7.3); Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests (weight 7.1); Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom (weight 7.1); Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed (weight 6.6); Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place (weight 6.6). evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A people is destroyed by the Shout / Blast (al-sayha) (weight 7.7); Refrain 'away with...' (bu'dan li-) the destroyed people (weight 7.1); The destroyed are as if they had never lived in their land (weight 6.8); Morning finds the destroyed lying prostrate (jathimin) in their dwellings (weight 6.6); Prophet's refrain to his people: 'Worship God; you have no god other than him' (weight 6.2). Pair score 34.5.

Only in Salih, the she-camel and the Shout: The people tell their prophet he had been their hope before this; After the crime the people are given three days' enjoyment in their homes before destruction; The people hamstring (slaughter) God's she-camel and so seal their doom; A she-camel of God is given as a sign; she must be left to graze unharmed; Unbelievers defend their practice as what they found their fathers doing; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil.

Only in Shu'ayb - measures, the prayer that commands, the clan: The people mock: 'Does your prayer command you that we abandon our fathers' gods or our way with our wealth?'; The prophet does not wish to do himself what he forbids them; he wants only reform; What God leaves you (baqiyyat Allah) is better than dishonest gain; Only the prophet's clan keeps the people from stoning him; Prophet tells deniers 'Wait, I too am waiting'; Roll call of destroyed peoples: Noah's, Ad, Thamud, Abraham's people, Midian and the overturned cities; Honest balances, weights, ephah and hin are commanded.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The chiefs (al-mala') of the prophet's people accuse him of error or folly and reject him (weight 7.1); Prophet's refrain to his people: 'Worship God; you have no god other than him' (weight 6.2); Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood (weight 6.2); Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger (weight 5.9); Hero's family saved with him (weight 5.4). Only in Noah warns his people: The drowned/destroyed were a blind people; Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger [divergence between the texts]; Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood [divergence between the texts]; People marvel that a reminder came through a man from among them; Prophet calls himself his people's sincere and trustworthy adviser (nasih amin); The righteous man's warning is taken as a joke by his own relatives; Hero's family saved with him [divergence between the texts].

Only in Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi: Embark: 'in the name of God be its sailing and its mooring'; God commands: 'Earth, swallow your water; sky, withhold!' and the water subsides; Noah reminds God that his son is of his family and God's promise is true; The elite scorn the prophet because only the lowest of them follow him; God answers that the drowned son is not of Noah's family: 'he is a deed not righteous'; The prophet's stories are 'tidings of the unseen' unknown to him and his people before; The ark sails through waves like mountains; The flood hero is blessed after the flood; the content of the blessing [divergence between the texts]; What the flood hero receives when he leaves the vessel [divergence between the texts]; A son who rejects his father's teaching is to be driven away: 'he is not your son, he was not born to you' [divergence between the texts]; The earth is addressed in the vocative and bidden to open, receive or swallow something [shared matter] [divergence between the texts]; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; and 37 more.

leads.title: Ziusudra (Eridu Genesis, ETCSL 1.7.4, segments C-E) ↔ Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi
leads.summary: 3 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Hero blessed on leaving the vessel (weight 6.2); Deity decides to destroy humankind (weight 6.1); Hero privately warned of the coming flood by a deity (weight 5.8). Pair score 18.2.

Only in Ziusudra (Eridu Genesis, ETCSL 1.7.4, segments C-E): The flood storm rages for seven days and seven nights; A goddess laments the destruction of the people decreed by the gods; The sun god appears after the flood and shines into the boat through an opening the hero makes; Animals taken aboard (no pairing specified); The gods grant the flood hero life like a god, eternal life; The flood hero is settled in a far land (Dilmun) where the sun rises; The gods are made to swear an oath binding them to the decision to destroy humankind; Warning spoken to a wall or reed hut so the hero overhears; The verdict of the divine assembly to destroy is declared irrevocable; Seventh ancestor walks with God and is taken without dying; Hero singled out as righteous or pious; Hero offers sacrifice after leaving the vessel; and 4 more.

Only in Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi: Embark: 'in the name of God be its sailing and its mooring'; God commands: 'Earth, swallow your water; sky, withhold!' and the water subsides; Noah reminds God that his son is of his family and God's promise is true; The elite scorn the prophet because only the lowest of them follow him; God answers that the drowned son is not of Noah's family: 'he is a deed not righteous'; The prophet's stories are 'tidings of the unseen' unknown to him and his people before; The ark sails through waves like mountains; The flood hero is blessed after the flood; the content of the blessing [divergence between the texts]; What the flood hero receives when he leaves the vessel [divergence between the texts]; A son who rejects his father's teaching is to be driven away: 'he is not your son, he was not born to you' [divergence between the texts]; The earth is addressed in the vocative and bidden to open, receive or swallow something [shared matter] [divergence between the texts]; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; and 39 more.

passages.text: فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
قُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ

وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصْبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٍ وَٰحِدٍ فَٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخْرِجْ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مِنۢ بَقْلِهَا وَقِثَّآئِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَا قَالَ أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِصْرًا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلْتُمْ وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ وَٱلْمَسْكَنَةُ وَبَآءُو بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يَكْفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّۦنَ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوا۟ وَّكَانُوا۟ يَعْتَدُونَ

ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِىَ كَٱلْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلْحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ ٱلْمَآءُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
قَالَ فَٱهْبِطْ مِنْهَا فَمَا يَكُونُ لَكَ أَن تَتَكَبَّرَ فِيهَا فَٱخْرُجْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰغِرِينَ
قَالَ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
قِيلَ يَٰنُوحُ ٱهْبِطْ بِسَلَٰمٍ مِّنَّا وَبَرَكَٰتٍ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ أُمَمٍ مِّمَّن مَّعَكَ وَأُمَمٌ سَنُمَتِّعُهُمْ ثُمَّ يَمَسُّهُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
قَالَ ٱهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۢا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ

passages.text: وَجَآءَهُۥ قَوْمُهُۥ يُهْرَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ وَمِن قَبْلُ كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ بَنَاتِى هُنَّ أَطْهَرُ لَكُمْ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُخْزُونِ فِى ضَيْفِىٓ أَلَيْسَ مِنكُمْ رَجُلٌ رَّشِيدٌ
وَنَبِّئْهُمْ عَن ضَيْفِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
قَالَ إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ضَيْفِى فَلَا تَفْضَحُونِ
هَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ
وَلَقَدْ رَٰوَدُوهُ عَن ضَيْفِهِۦ فَطَمَسْنَآ أَعْيُنَهُمْ فَذُوقُوا۟ عَذَابِى وَنُذُرِ

passages.text: قَالُوا۟ يَٰشُعَيْبُ مَا نَفْقَهُ كَثِيرًا مِّمَّا تَقُولُ وَإِنَّا لَنَرَىٰكَ فِينَا ضَعِيفًا وَلَوْلَا رَهْطُكَ لَرَجَمْنَٰكَ وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيْنَا بِعَزِيزٍ
قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ أَرَهْطِىٓ أَعَزُّ عَلَيْكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَٱتَّخَذْتُمُوهُ وَرَآءَكُمْ ظِهْرِيًّا إِنَّ رَبِّى بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطٌ
وَكَانَ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ تِسْعَةُ رَهْطٍ يُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا يُصْلِحُونَ

leads.title: tannūr: the oven that boiled at the Flood
leads.summary: Akkadian tinūru (oven) reached Aramaic, Hebrew, and Arabic. In the Quran's Noah narrative the sign of the Flood is that the tannūr boiled over.

passages.text: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ قُلْنَا ٱحْمِلْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ وَمَنْ ءَامَنَ وَمَآ ءَامَنَ مَعَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ

فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ
